lines.text: Every maple on the near side has a bucket on it. It is October.
Sap runs when it freezes at night and thaws by day. Six weeks of that, come March. Not now.
Somebody up here has noticed the nights, and hung their buckets. Good for them. I wish they hadn't needed to.
A long flat stone, worn hollow in the middle. Bearers set the coffin down here and got their breath before the last climb.
That's a long way to carry anyone, when there's a good churchyard on the Green. They must have wanted to lie near something.
MERCY WHITCOMB. Beloved wife. Gone before the frost.
JOTHAM TUTTLE. He wound the church clock for sixty years. The rest has worn away.
OBADIAH THAYER. He set the last course, and was paid.
Thayer. There are Thayers at Hardscrabble still. I'd like to know in what coin.
No family name. No dates. Someone has left a stone on top, and it isn't old.
No words at all. A ring cut deep, and three strokes under it.
Three crossed lines is the Warden's mark. This isn't that. This is what that was copied from.
